lesson_title: Why a Triangle Is Half a Rectangle
hook_text: Every triangle is exactly half a rectangle. Watch the corners fold in.
clip_script: Draw the triangle inside a rectangle with the same base and the same height. The triangle fills exactly half of the rectangle: the parts of the rectangle outside the triangle can be cut and fitted together to make a second copy of the triangle. So the triangle's area is half of base times height. The triangular flag has a base of forty centimetres and a perpendicular height of thirty centimetres. Area: half of forty times thirty, 600 square centimetres.
visual_style: A triangular flag inside a 40 by 30 rectangle; the two empty corners slide together into a second flag; 1 200 halves to 600.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to master area and perimeter formulae.
